A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same research, renamed from 3DSwapping to 3DOT. Their text, equations, figures and tables support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both reference separate supplementary material that is not supplied.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative comparisons, user-study ratings, qualitative texture-transfer results and guidance ablations in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds quantitative component ablations and editing-time measurements in Sections 4.2–4.3.

M1.justification: v2 adds an alternative reference-construction route using directly cropped or pasted textures. Section 3.3 also changes token initialization from random initialization to initialization using a base prompt. These are limited procedural revisions; the three main components and their losses and guidance equations remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate face-forwarding and 360-degree scenes involving color, material and larger semantic texture edits. The added ablations and timing measurements do not establish new dataset or task coverage. Geometry-mismatch tolerance is discussed without a new reported evaluation.

E2.justification: Table 1 and the corresponding qualitative comparisons retain IN2N, IGS2GS, GaussCtrl and DGE; Figure 1 retains Plug-n-Play. The new speed comparison reuses GaussCtrl and IN2N. StyleSplat is newly discussed but not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 introduces editing-time evaluation and additional controls that disable prompt guidance or replace progressive propagation with editing from only the initial reference. The principal benchmark metrics and five-point user-rating procedure remain unchanged. Revised user-study scores do not establish a changed participant count or study design.

E4.justification: v1 provides qualitative guidance analyses but no quantitative component-ablation table. v2 adds Table 2 separately removing all three components, including the first explicit progressive-generation ablation. Figure 6a adds prompt-guidance removal and replaces the baby-face consistency example with a bear example; the two-reference prompt analysis is retained in compressed form.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. The added result rows and changed user-study means do not change uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: All five Table 1 user-study means change, including Ours from 4.5400 to 4.5750; the four automated-metric rows remain identical. v2 adds quantitative ablation results in Table 2 and editing times of 23min 33s for Ours, 15min 47s for GaussCtrl and 20h 51min 20s for IN2N. These are newly reported results, not demonstrated same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The attention, diffusion, texture-difference and prompt-loss formulations in Equations 1–8 are substantively unchanged. v2 adds explanations and informal applicability qualifications, but no new formal derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v2 removes the abstract's categorical statement that no dedicated method exists and recasts the conclusion's 'new capability' as an underexplored capability. The central contributions—single-image texture transfer, three guidance/generation components and superiority to the evaluated baselines—remain.

C2.justification: v1 treats differently shaped references as incompatible and potentially destabilizing. v2 instead distinguishes tolerable minor mismatches from larger mismatches addressed through reference regeneration, explaining proposed correction mechanisms. It also adds a segmentation-based explanation of dark borders and a multi-view-diffusion incompatibility argument, while removing the explicit caveat about prompt-training oscillations.

D1.justification: v2 newly states that the pipeline typically uses two image-editing iterations and reports total and per-iteration guidance overhead. The abstract replaces a promise of code upon acceptance with a project-page link, although the PDF does not establish code availability. Hardware and detailed experimental settings remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through a new StyleSplat discussion and a dedicated comparison with multi-view diffusion, emphasizing editing an existing 3D representation. It adds literature on 3DGS, scene representations, segmentation and depth, and removes several references associated with v1's proposed 2D-editing workaround for mismatched geometry.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method explanations are extensively rewritten, with terminology changed throughout from swapping to texture transfer and the method renamed 3DOT. Quantitative and qualitative evaluation are merged under Section 4.1, a speed subsection is introduced, and the discussion is reorganized into named topics.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document from two columns to one and substantially recomposes the qualitative displays, including replacing full-size secondary face views with insets. The earlier ten-view prompt analysis is reduced to two views in Figure 6b, the baby-face ablation figure is replaced, and a new quantitative ablation table is added.

improvement.justification: Table 2 provides useful quantitative evidence for the three components, including progressive generation, and Section 4.2 makes the editing-cost tradeoff explicit. The expanded failure discussion also improves practical understanding. These gains remain limited by sparse ablation and timing settings, unexplained user-study revisions, and a new Figure 6b caption that reverses the reference-image roles stated in Section 4.3.
